listLocalAddresses.o_.label: Auto (use local-network preferred)
globalSettings.s_mode.title: Tunnel Mode
globalSettings.s_mode.mode.label: Mode
globalSettings.s_mode.mode.description: Quick: random *.trycloudflare.com URL, no account. Custom: server-managed named tunnel on your own domain (requires a Cloudflare account + API token). Hit Start on the Remote Access page to launch — Custom mode auto-provisions on first start. The local hub port is auto-detected from CAMSTACK_PORT / PORT env.
globalSettings.s_mode.mode.o_quick.label: Quick Tunnel
globalSettings.s_mode.localHost.label: Local Address
globalSettings.s_mode.localHost.descript: Which local host address cloudflared should forward traffic to. "Auto" follows the local-network preferred interface — pin a specific address only when running multi-NIC or Docker sidecar setups.
globalSettings.s_custom.title: Custom Domain Setup
globalSettings.s_custom.customHelp.label: How to get an API token
globalSettings.s_custom.customApiToken.d: Used to provision + manage the tunnel.
globalSettings.s_custom.customZoneId.des: Pick the Cloudflare zone (root domain) the tunnel will sit on.
globalSettings.s_custom.customHostname.d: Sub-domain to prepend to the selected zone (e.g. "camstack" → camstack.yourdomain.com). Use "@" or empty for the apex.
globalSettings.s_custom.localPortMode.de: Default: the addon resolves the hub backend port automatically (CAMSTACK_PORT, fallback 4443 HTTPS). Pick "Custom" only when you need to forward to a non-default service.
globalSettings.s_custom.localPort.label: Port
globalSettings.s_custom.localPort.descri: Local HTTPS port cloudflared forwards to. Must accept https:// requests (the addon adds noTLSVerify to handle the self-signed cert).
globalSettings.s_custom.noTLSVerify.desc: Cloudflared accepts the origin TLS cert without checking the CA chain. Required when the hub serves HTTPS with a self-signed cert (default for camstack).
globalSettings.s_custom.originServerName: Server Name Indication sent during the TLS handshake. Leave empty unless the origin cert is issued for a specific hostname different from the LAN address.
globalSettings.s_custom.httpHostHeader.d: Force a specific Host header on requests forwarded to the origin. Leave empty to pass the public hostname through.
globalSettings.s_custom.pruneStaleTunnel: Runs an audit on the Cloudflare account: lists every "camstack"-named tunnel, deletes any that aren't the currently-active one, and rewrites the public CNAME if it points at a stale tunnel id. Use when the public domain returns "Cloudflare Tunnel error 1033".
globalSettings.s_diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
globalSettings.s_diagnostics.debugLoggin: Pass --loglevel debug --transport-loglevel debug to cloudflared. Respawns the tunnel.
globalSettings.s_diagnostics.protocol.de: Force the cloudflared ↔ Cloudflare-edge transport. Auto = cloudflared default (usually QUIC). HTTP/2 = fall back to TCP+TLS with HTTP/2 multiplexing, useful when QUIC stream-stall causes individual requests to queue for seconds under burst. Respawns the tunnel.
globalSettings.s_credentials.title: Cloudflare Credentials
globalSettings.s_credentials.description: API credentials for fetching TURN relay tokens from Cloudflare Realtime.
globalSettings.s_credentials.turnHelp.la: How to get the TURN Key ID + API Token
globalSettings.s_credentials.accountId.d: Token ID of the Realtime TURN app (NOT your Cloudflare Account ID — it's a separate hex id generated when you create the TURN app).
globalSettings.s_credentials.apiToken.de: The API Token shown alongside the Token ID when you created the TURN app. App-scoped — separate from any Cloudflare global API token.
globalSettings.s_credentials.testCredent: Hit the Cloudflare TURN API with the current Key ID + API Token. On success shows the URL count + whether credentials came back; on failure shows the raw response with an operator hint.
